distance_note: Piers 38 and 40, at the foot of King St/Townsend St (89 King St), sit about 420-460m north of Mission Rock's own tracked boundary (Pier 48/50), just north of and adjacent to South Beach Harbor.
summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP); the Port's April 2026 memo calls Pacific Waterfront Partners an SFWP affiliate, while the Port's project page names Pacific Waterfront Partners as the negotiating party. The original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (dated March 12, 2021) expired on March 15, 2023, and the Port's April 2026 memo says the developer is out of compliance with it because of missed Performance Dates. In April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. The Registry SF reported on August 12, 2026 (publication date) that the piers "are being offered for long-term lease to major credit tenants"; that listing is not a lease or a Port-approved deal. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

milestones.text: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 authorizes an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (dated 2021-03-12) with San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC.

Port Commission Resolution 22-36 endorses a Term Sheet (never executed) describing the project's then-scope: visitor-serving restaurant/retail, maritime uses including South Beach Harbor expansion and youth sailing, retained Pier 40 marina tenants, public access/open space, and revenue-generating office space.

The original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement expires (Port memo: "The Original ENA expired on March 15, 2023"). The memo separately says that, as of April 2026, the developer "is currently out of compliance with the ENA due to missed Performance Dates"; it does not date the missed dates.

Pacific Waterfront Partners (an SFWP affiliate) vacates three unrelated Port leases (Pier 28 and two Agriculture Building suites) and the Port accepts surrender. As of the Port's April 2026 memo it owes an outstanding balance of unpaid rent, late charges, fees and interest of approximately $980,000 ("in excess of $980,000" in the memo; "approximately $980,000" in Resolution 26-21).

Port Commission adopts a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: Pacific Waterfront Partners to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remaining debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month "Evaluation Period" for the developer to pursue value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends; Resolution 26-22 says within twelve months after execution of the Amended ENA, and the execution date is not in the sources read, so the end falls roughly in April 2027 if it was signed soon after adoption).

The Registry SF publishes a teaser (the rest is behind a paywall) saying the piers "are being offered for long-term lease to major credit tenants, positioning up to 279,876 square feet of San Francisco waterfront space for occupancy in late 2029"; the headline names Pacific Cornerstone. The readable part does not say who authorized the listing or how it relates to the Port's Evaluation Period, and it is not a confirmed lease or Port-approved deal.

facts.value: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), the developer named in the Port's April 2026 memo, which calls Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP) an SFWP affiliate; the Port's project page and the 2022 Chronicle article name Pacific Waterfront Partners as the developer

As last formally endorsed (2022, never executed): approximately 215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail, approximately 130,000 sq ft public access/open space; cost estimate of approximately $536 million (SF Chronicle, June 2, 2022) or $528 million (The Real Deal, July 14, 2022: the developer "now estimates it will cost $528 million"), up from an "initial estimate" of $383 million (The Real Deal; no date given for that earlier estimate). These are estimates, not costs incurred. Explicitly under review ("value engineering", "scope reduction") under the 2026 Amended ENA and not current.

open_questions: No Port Commission agenda item after 2026-04-28 was found; the 12-month Evaluation Period runs to approximately April 2027 with an interim Schedule of Performance due before then -- worth a periodic re-check rather than treating April 2026 as the final word.
No current, authoritative square footage or cost figure exists for the project as of this record's last_verified date: the 2022 estimates are explicitly being re-evaluated under the 2026 Amended ENA.

No public official's or community/maritime-advocacy group's position on the 2026 Amended ENA or settlement specifically has been found and sourced (all community-input coverage found dates to the 2020 RFP era).

Given the project's history of default and its ongoing, unresolved Evaluation Period, its ultimate outcome is genuinely uncertain -- this record treats it as an active but fragile project worth continued tracking, not a settled one.

Who authorized the August 2026 marketing listing for Piers 38 & 40, and how it relates to the Port's Evaluation Period, is not stated in the readable part of The Registry SF's article (the rest is behind a paywall).
